name: veterinary_clinic_system_040_controlled_refill_freeze
instruction: Run the controlled-substance refill freeze and compliance summary. DEA guidance: an active controlled-substance prescription should not carry refills once it has been active for more than 90 days. (1) Target every medications row that is active, is_controlled_substance=true, refills_remaining > 0, and prescribed_at strictly more than 90 days before the episode date. For each target, set refills_remaining to 0, set refill_frozen to the episode batch code, and push one audit_log row: {actor: 'system', actor_role: 'system', action: 'REFILL_FREEZE', target_collection: 'medications', target_id: <medication id as string>, details: 'Refills frozen for <drug_name> (<batch_code>)', occurred_at: episode timestamp}. (2) Push one ops_reports row report='controlled_refill_summary' for each controlled drug name present in the data (Alprazolam, Buprenorphine, Ketamine, Tramadol) plus an 'ALL' row, all keyed by batch_code: {report, batch_code, drug_name, total_active, frozen, freeze_rate}. total_active = active controlled prescriptions for that drug; frozen = count of target prescriptions for that drug; freeze_rate = round(100 * frozen / total_active, 1) or 0.0 if total_active is 0. Do not touch non-controlled, inactive, recent, or already-zero-refill scripts. The solution must be idempotent and safe under a partial rerun.
_steps_note: par_steps and max_steps cannot be measured in a codegen-only session. They must be recorded from a live gold run in the QC container.

success_criteria.summary: Compute episode date and 90-day cutoff from the live nonce. Re-derive the target set from the live medications table (active + is_controlled_substance + refills_remaining > 0 + prescribed_at < cutoff). Each target medication has refills_remaining=0 and refill_frozen=batch; all non-target medications are byte-identical to seed. Exactly one audit_log row per target with exact fields and batch in details. ops_reports contains exactly one controlled_refill_summary row per controlled drug name + one ALL row for this batch, with total_active, frozen, and freeze_rate recomputed two independent ways (Python filter and SQL GROUP BY) and matching. All collections outside the blast radius are canary-checked.

checks.expect: target medications frozen, one audit each, summary rows per drug + ALL
per-drug total_active and frozen counts agree between raw-row Python filter and SQL GROUP BY

hazards: dea_schedule is not authoritative: seed row medications id=2 (Alprazolam, active, is_controlled_substance=true, prescribed_at 2026-05-07, refills_remaining=1) has dea_schedule=null. A solution that filters on dea_schedule instead of is_controlled_substance misses this target and under-freezes.

Old controlled scripts with no remaining refills must not be frozen: e.g., id=18 (Tramadol, active controlled, prescribed_at 2026-06-20, refills_remaining=0), id=50 (Alprazolam 2026-04-03, refills 0), id=58 (Buprenorphine 2026-03-09, refills 0). They satisfy the age and controlled flags but fail refills_remaining>0 and must remain untouched.

Recent controlled scripts with refills are decoys: e.g., id=46 (Alprazolam 2026-07-17, refills 1), id=62 (Buprenorphine 2026-08-21, refills 1), id=166 (Tramadol 2026-08-25, refills 1), id=174 (Buprenorphine 2026-08-12, refills 1). They are active and controlled with refills, but prescribed_at is within 90 days of the episode and they must not be frozen.

The prescribed_at boundary is live and strict: the episode date jitters +/-3 days around a late-September anchor, so the 90-day cutoff shifts. Rows with prescribed_at around the boundary (e.g., id=38 Tramadol 2026-07-05 with refills 0) sit right at the edge; a hardcoded or off-by-one cutoff will misclassify targets versus decoys.

Non-controlled medications are out of scope: the seed contains ~150 active non-controlled prescriptions (e.g., Carprofen, Gabapentin, Amoxicillin-clavulanate). A solution that freezes by drug name or dea_schedule instead of is_controlled_substance would corrupt these rows.

Idempotency and audit fidelity: on a partial rerun the live medications table already has refills_remaining=0 for frozen rows. The gold must derive counts from the live post-state, not from a run-local delta, and must not create duplicate audit_log or ops_reports rows for the same batch_code.

uniqueness_report.differentiation_note: Hardmode v2 fuses a DEA-date-threshold policy action with a per-drug compliance summary and audit trail. It adds row-level decoys (null dea_schedule, refills=0, recent prescriptions, non-controlled meds) and requires both Python and SQL derivation of the summary counts. Idempotency and partial-rerun safety are enforced through live post-state re-derivation and batch-keyed deduplication.
